title: WorkspaceOnboardingForm
wrapsNative: VStack of MonarchTextField, MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput, MonarchRadioCardGroup and MonarchButton, with @State for values and validation
summary: A recipe, not a component: the form that creates a workspace, with a name, a unique username checked for availability, and a workspace type, with inline validation and a pending submit.
whenToUse: In the first-run flow of a product that needs a workspace or organisation before anything else.
whenNotToUse: Not for editing an existing workspace's settings (use a Form with sections) and not for signing up a person (that is the account flow).
api: VStack { MonarchTextField("Workspace name", text: $name, error: nameError); MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput("Workspace username", text: $username, prefix: "@", onStatusChange: …, validate: …); MonarchRadioCardGroup("Type", selection: $type, options: …, columns: 2); MonarchButton("Continue", variant: .primary, isLoading: isCreating, fullWidth: true) { … } }

states.name: invalid name
states.description: MonarchTextField shows the error once the person has typed or submitted: at least 4 and at most 25 characters.

states.name: username checking, available, taken or failed
states.description: MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput checks the local rules and the product's lookup after typing pauses, and reports its status; Continue waits for valid.

states.name: type missing
states.description: After a submit without a type, an error label with an icon appears under the cards.

states.name: creating
states.description: The Continue button shows a progress indicator while the product creates the workspace.

appearance: Each part keeps its own Monarch look: the text field's input border, the radio cards' selected border and mark, the primary button. Errors use the danger strong role with an icon.
platformNotes: The web ships WorkspaceOnboardingForm as one pattern with onSubmit, checkUsername, rules and messages props. On iOS it is a recipe: the fields, rules and submit logic stay in the app's view, so the rules (4 to 25 characters for the name, 5 to 30 letters and digits for the username) and the default types (Creator and Business) are shown in the example and are not a Monarch API. The web's form error alert after a failed submit is left to the app, for example MonarchInlineNotice above the button.
accessibility: Each field keeps its own label, helper and error text, read by VoiceOver with the field.
The username status is announced by MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput.
The type cards are buttons with the selected trait.
Errors have an icon and text, not colour alone.
The Continue button reports its loading state.
edgeCases: Submitting while the username is still being checked does nothing; tell the person to wait, as the catalogue page does.
At the accessibility text sizes the two type cards stack in one column.
